title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost illegible: the ink is very faint, and in places the text seems erased or lightly crossed out. What can be read (the opening 'Soient E, K deux extensions de Q', 'E ⊗_Q K̄ = E_K ⊗_K K̄', 'Spec E_K̄ ≅ Homalg(E, K̄)', 'σ(Σ)=Σ', 'gτg^{-1}(Σ)=Σ', 'H', a circled '§2' in the margin) shows it is an earlier draft of the §2 written out on the next page (146). That section is 'CM-structures on E relative to K'.

Setting: E and K are extensions of Q, and 𝔄 is an ideal of E⊗_Q K. Over a closure K̄, 𝔄 gives a subset Σ of Spec(E⊗_Q K̄) = Hom(E, K̄). 𝔄 is called a CM-structure on E relative to K if every 'conjugation' τ ∈ G = Gal(K̄/K) (an element induced by a complex conjugation) sends Σ to its complement.

Consequence drawn in the text: for g ∈ G, gτg^{-1} is again a conjugation, so gτg^{-1}Σ = complement = τΣ. Hence τ^{-1}gτg^{-1} fixes Σ. So Σ is stable under the closed normal subgroup H generated by these commutators. The field of definition K_0 of 𝔄 (later called k_Σ, essentially the reflex field) is therefore contained in the fixed field of H. In that field complex conjugation is central, so it lies inside the maximal CM extension Q^{cm}. K_0 is non-real, since τΣ ≠ Σ (Hom(E, K̄) being nonempty).

In the Galois-set picture over Q̄: E and K correspond to G_Q-sets I_E and I_K. The ideal 𝔄 is a G-invariant subset of I_E × I_K, and the condition is (τ×1)Σ_y = I_E − Σ_y on the fibre over a base point y.

This is the generalized CM-type / reflex-field formalism of Shimura–Taniyama, with values in an arbitrary base K. It serves the preceding pages, which construct the Serre group S_K, the weight homomorphism G_m → S_K with ε∘i = λ², and conjectures identifying it with the motivic Galois group of CM motives.
errors: The condition only concerns conjugations lying in Gal(K̄/K). If K has no real embedding there are none, and the definition becomes vacuous (every Σ qualifies). This may be intended, but it is not remarked on.
The legible draft contains no other checkable mathematics; nothing wrong is visible.

ideas.what: CM-type (CM-structure) on a field E with values in an arbitrary base K, encoded as an ideal of E⊗_Q K such that complex conjugations exchange Σ and its complement
ideas.modern_name: CM type / generalized CM type; Galois-set formulation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (1961); in this generality Serre (1968), Deligne, Milne

ideas.what: Σ is invariant under the normal subgroup generated by the commutators [τ,g], so its field of definition lies in the CM part of Q̄

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faint, superseded draft of the next page's definition of CM-structures. It is standard CM-type/reflex material, now well documented in Serre, Deligne and Milne. Historically it is consistent with Grothendieck working on the Serre group/Taniyama-type questions around 1965, but this page adds nothing beyond page 146.
transcription_corrections: The page is a faint (largely erased) earlier version of §2 on page 146. The margin bears a circled '§2'. The first line reads approximately 'Soient E, K deux extensions de Q, 𝔄 un idéal de E⊗K, K̄ une clôture algébrique de K'. Later lines include 'définit une CM-structure sur E relativement à K', 'Spec E_K̄ ≃ Homalg(E,K̄)', 'G = Gal(K̄/K) qui est une conjugaison', 'Notons que ceci implique', 'gτg^{-1}(Σ) = ... = τΣ', 'τ^{-1}gτg^{-1}(Σ)=Σ', 'sous-groupe fermé invariant H'.
The fragment '(Q × Gal(K̄/K))' is likely '(G = Gal(K̄/K))'.
